root.name: Pterodactyl Defense: Sicilian, Siroccopteryx
root.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c5 4. Nf3 Qa5 5. Bc4

overview: Black fianchettoes the king's bishop, plays ...c5 and puts the queen on a5 early, pressuring the c3 knight and e5/c3 squares. After 5.Bc4 White develops quickly and eyes f7, while Black goes ...Nf6 and ...cxd4 or ...e6 to counterattack in a Sicilian-style fight. Black accepts early queen exposure for counterplay on the c-file and long diagonal.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bc4, O-O and Bf4/Be3 and play against the early queen
Capture on c5 or break with e5 if Black is not careful
Pressure f7 and the d5 square

black_ideas.idea: Use the queen on a5 to pin Nc3 and prepare ...cxd4
Counterattack with ...Nf6 and ...O-O, trading when needed

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian-type pawn structure with open c-file and White centre
Black bishop on g7 on the long diagonal

character.notes: Early queen and fianchetto against a central pawn pair; positions are unbalanced with real tactical risk for Black.

gambit.notes: No material is given, though ...cxd4 lines can be sharp.

soundness.notes: Considered playable with exact play; not a refutation.

structure.notes: Sicilian-style pawn structure with a half-open c-file.

approach.notes: Rare; strong players seldom play the Pterodactyl, which is chosen for surprise.

level.notes: Black must handle the early queen and avoid tactics; understanding rather than long theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5.dxc5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 c5 4. Nf3 Qa5 5. dxc5
sublines_that_differ.how: White takes the pawn; Black must regain it with ...Bxc3+ or ...Qxc5 ideas.

character.reason: Early queen sortie and counterplay against White's centre; unbalanced.

level.reason: Requires care with the early queen.

plans.reason: Bishop on g7 and queen on a5.
